goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer to an ActiveRecord association method that expects model instances, causing member removal to raise instead of deleting

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` at line 73 in admin/groups_controller.rb where `user_id` is an integer from `params.require(:user_id).to_i`. The ActiveRecord `has_many` association's `delete` method expects model instances or an array of model instances, not integer IDs. Passing an integer ID will not work as expected - it won't find and delete the user from the association. The correct approach would be to find the user first or use `group.users.where(id: user_id).delete_all` or similar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — create ignores the submitted alias_level, silently discarding the selected alias level

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the create method in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb lines 22-31, the code only sets group.name and group.visible from params, but does not set group.alias_level. In contrast, the update method at line 38 does set 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?'. This means if a user submits an alias_level when creating a group, it will be silently ignored. The template (group.hbs) shows the alias level selector is present in the form, so users would expect it to be saved on create.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit has no upper bound or positive-value validation, allowing arbitrarily large membership lists to be requested and serialized

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb line 22: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` - this takes user input directly and converts to integer without any upper bound validation. A malicious user could pass limit=1000000 to request and serialize an arbitrarily large membership list, potentially causing performance issues or denial of service. This is a security/performance bug as there's no maximum limit enforced.
